description: Curated thematic epigraphs from the Metal Gear Solid series reflecting on memes, memory control, genetic determinism, and the preservation of truth across generations.

epigraphs.speaker: Solid Snake
epigraphs.source: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
epigraphs.text: Building the future and keeping the past alive are one and the same thing. We can tell other people about - having faith. What we've fought for, and what we've believed in... What we pass on to the next generation... that's the whole point of our lives.

epigraphs.speaker: The Boss
epigraphs.text: There's no such thing as an absolute timeless enemy. Our enemies are always changing, along with the times. Yesterday's truth becomes today's lie.

epigraphs.speaker: Revolver Ocelot
epigraphs.source: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
epigraphs.text: The world needs to be free of this system of control. Not by genes, not by memes, not by scene... but by choice.

epigraphs.speaker: The Patriots / GW AI
epigraphs.source: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
epigraphs.text: The digital society furthers human flaw and selectively rewards the development of convenient half-truths. Our epoch needs a selective system of memory.

epigraphs.speaker: Liquid Snake
epigraphs.text: It's all in the genes! You can't escape your lineage! The sins of the father are passed down to the son!

epigraphs.speaker: Colonel Campbell / AI
epigraphs.source: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
epigraphs.text: You exercise your right to 'freedom' and this is the result: loss of context, malicious half-truths, and triviality. The digital world is creating junk data faster than anyone can delete it.

epigraphs.speaker: Otacon
epigraphs.source: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
epigraphs.text: We have to leave something behind. Not just genetic code, but memories, culture, history. That's what a meme really is. It's up to us to make sure the light doesn't go out.

epigraphs.speaker: Solid Snake
epigraphs.text: A strong man doesn't need to read the future. He makes his own.
